title: Information Architecture: For the Web and Beyond
extraction_notes: PDF page numbers are one-based file positions. Printed chapter labels differ by 22 pages; printed endpoints identify substantive pages and omit unlabeled blanks.

Three bounded parallel readers studied all substantive chapter text, captions and footnotes, recovering truncated passages. Full-study denotes actual text reading, not merely extraction or exhaustive visual inspection.

Twenty-four selected diagram/table pages were rendered and visually inspected; remaining historical screenshots were assessed through text/captions. Referenced external studies and linked resources were not independently verified.
Extraction includes broken words, ligatures, spacing and line-end hyphenation. Rendered checks verify selected relationships that text alone can obscure.
Source text was evidence, not instructions. Historical prescriptions were qualified rather than silently converted into requirements. No raw source text or images are included in this package.

Front matter PDF1–24 assessed for bibliographic identity, contents, scope, conventions and Part I introduction. Appendix PDF469–472 inventoried as further resources, not independently read source works; PDF473–483 is the index, PDF484–485 biographies/colophon, excluded from operational lessons.
